requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was initially absent, then created with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash. It remained present with the correct home ownership after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: Direct PAM-backed login-session checks showed both soft and hard nofile limits of 8192 and nproc limits of 256. The same effective limits and unchanged configuration checksum were observed after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed from 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8 to 30d42084-a41d-4029-89df-cfab02d61fa0, and SSH, the account, home directory, configuration, and effective login limits recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the identity change.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not independently inventory local accounts or limits files; those outcomes are instead established by direct pre- and post-restart executor observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the account and limits file was required (cmd-05dfcb3e823948a0), while the scheduled reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol (cmd-d0e9109432334d14). The other commands were bounded verification or restart polling. Post-executor observations showed no failed services, damaged package state, new exposure, or abandoned temporary residue; temporary-directory and SSH PID changes were ordinary consequences of the verified reboot.
